messages:
ashok: Quick ask — need a small perf smoke focused on tok/s and p95 after the KV-cache patch landed. Can someone run a quick bench or point me to the dashboard slices to check regression? Want to gate the canary.
james: Which model/config and representative traffic? small vs med seq matters a lot here.
sophiar: I can run a short job on the dedicated pool. Which metric names should I compare? TTFT or first-token p95?
ashok: Thanks. Target is redwood-v1-8b (fp16, no quant), seq=2048 typical, batch=1 tail SLO: p95 < 250ms, tok/s baseline around 1200 on that pool. Focus on: first-token latency (TTFT), overall p95, and tokens/sec (client-visible). Also check cold vs warm cache.
maria: For dashboard slices, compare recent-canary vs prod-24h. Use sampling window 10m, agg p95. Also check tok/s computed as tokens / total_runtime, not tokens / server_time (we had mismatch last time).
kevin: Dashboard tiles: "runtime.first_token_ms.p95", "runtime.p95_ms", "runtime.tokens_per_second". If you want a direct query, try PromQL snippet:
```
max_over_time(runtime_first_token_ms_p95{model="redwood-v1-8b",pool="dedicated-us-east"}[10m])
rate(runtime_tokens_total{model="redwood-v1-8b"}[1m])
```
That gives you the p95 spike and tokens/sec rate.
ben: FYI tokenization differences can swing tokens/sec by 5-8% between clients — make sure the pump input is canonicalized (same tokenizer + prompt). Also set kv-cache warm path: run 3 seeds to stabilize.
ashok: Good catch @ben. I'll attach the exact prompt and seed list. Also would like a lightweight regression alert: if p95 increases >10% vs baseline over a 30m window, ping #eng-runtime and post here.
sophiar: I'll kick off bench now. Using the perf harness with these flags:
```
./perf-harness --model redwood-v1-8b --seq 2048 --batch 1 --workers 16 --warmups 3 --run 600
```
Posting raw numbers back.
perf-bot: job 1851234590 started on dedicated-us-east (run id: rb-1851). :rocket:
ashok: thx. if anyone can also spot-check the dashboard slices + trace for a couple slow requests that'd be great (trace ids are helpful to see kernel scheduling vs queuing).
james: If you want traces, enable trace sampling = 1% for bench or run 10 debug requests with trace=1 to avoid noise.
sophiar: Run finished. Summary (quick): first-token p95 increased 6% vs baseline, overall p95 increased 12% (this is over the 10% threshold). tokens/sec dropped ~9%.
perf-bot: Summary for run rb-1851: first_token_p95=138ms (baseline=130ms), p95=312ms (baseline=280ms), tokens_per_second=1090 (baseline=1200). Artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/rb-1851/{metrics,flamegraphs,traces}
maria: Looks like p95 regression crosses the 10% threshold. @eng-runtime Could we revert the KV-cache change on the canary or apply the staged fallback? Also upload the flamegraph and one trace here.
ashok: Agreed. @ops, can we hold the canary rollout and roll back the patch? I'll open a revert PR and paste link here.
ben: I'll inspect the flamegraphs — quick hypothesis: more CPU on tokenization path due to extra copying in the new cache code.
james: If that's true, a micro-optimization (move memcpy out of hot loop) should fix tok/s and reduce p95. I can draft a patch.
sophiar: Reuploading artifacts: s3 link above has flamegraph.svg and trace.json. Sharing top-level flame excerpt in thread. :eyes:
ashok: Great. Thanks everyone for the quick turn. We'll coordinate on the revert PR and follow-up perf patch. If anyone else runs checks, paste results in this thread so we have a single source of truth. :white_check_mark:
